clue.text: Cricketer Bunyan named Goodwill

definitions.meaning: a fielder who stands behind the stumps to catch and stump
in The Pilgrim's Progress, John Bunyan's Goodwill is the man who guards and opens the wicket gate

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the gloved fielder behind the stumps in cricket; the other is Bunyan's gatekeeper at the small wicket gate in his allegory.

clue.text: Babbles like those battered when the heat's turned on

definitions.meaning: talks at length without saying much

definitions.text: like those battered when the heat's turned on
definitions.meaning: batter cakes cooked in a hot grid-patterned iron

explanation.definitionFit: Rambling on aimlessly is one sense; the other is grid-patterned batter cakes baked between hot iron plates.

clue.text: Sing low — no whale is up to it

indicators.note: in a down clue being up means read from the bottom, so the words no and whale are turned around

parts.note: taken as written
an orc is a killer whale

explanation.surface: Nobody can sing that low, says a whale who is not up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reverses NOORC, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hum or sing softly in a low tone, as a crooner does.

clue.text: Flora's good feeling about a bee?

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: euphoria is a strong feeling of well-being
bee is how the letter B is spelt out

explanation.surface: Flora feels happy about a bumble bee in her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name, but it means plant life; 'about' puts B inside EUPHORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurge genus is a large group of plants, so it belongs to the flora of a region.

clue.text: The bird's. strung up

parts.note: a bird of prey, and also a paper toy flown high on a string, so the bird name goes up on a line

explanation.definitionFit: A fork-tailed hawk shares its name with the toy flown aloft on a string.

clue.text: A mere oriental painter

parts.note: east is oriental
a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: Just an artist from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only' but is the noun for a lake; Sir Charles Eastlake was a Victorian painter and gallery director.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Charles Eastlake was an English artist and President of the Royal Academy.

clue.text: Did she do a Limey wrong.?

indicators.note: doing something wrong scrambles it, so the letters of Limey are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was it a woman who cheated an Englishman?
explanation.walkthrough: Limey is American slang for a British person.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: After depression maybe I can render old pop song of Spain

indicators.note: after says the next piece comes behind the first

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

indicators.note: render means turn into another form, so I and can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling low, a singer belts out an old Spanish hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'render' shuffles 'I can' to follow the valley word. 'Valencia' was a 1926 dance hit named after the Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1926 dance hit was named after the Spanish city and region on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: First 'and last Harry's a bit of a soak, Herb

parts.note: the first and last letters of Harry are H and Y, followed by the S of the possessive
a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid

explanation.surface: Harry has a small sip first and last, then calls it herbal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushy aromatic plant of the mint family is used in cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Ways to avoid traffic

parts.note: routes meant for walkers, where pedestrians keep clear of cars; 'avoid' is not a planning instruction but what these paths let you do

explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian tracks are routes reserved for walking, away from vehicles on the road.

clue.text: The laity troubled about Rome

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up and disturbed, so the letters of laity are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers are worried about the Vatican's line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' looks like the Church the laity worries over, but the definition is 'about Rome': the country all around the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The country surrounding the capital city is the land in which that city sits.

clue.text: Savage country where gold is found

parts.note: a land is a country
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wild land where prospectors strike gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savage' looks like an adjective for the country, but it is the middle name of the poet Walter Savage Landor.
explanation.definitionFit: The English poet Walter Savage Landor carried this middle name, so the clue names him by it.

clue.text: " Brief Lives'" by Jaques'?

parts.note: Jaques in As You Like It says all the world's a stage and each man in his time plays many parts, so a short life is a little drama

explanation.definitionFit: If every life is a play, as Jaques says, then brief lives are short dramatic pieces.

clue.text: Scraps as daily

definitions.meaning: what a daily (a British term for a cleaning lady who comes in each day) does to floors

explanation.definitionFit: To call off a plan is informally to cancel it; a charwoman also cleans by hard rubbing with a brush.

clue.text: Drink to get a boxer groggy

definitions.meaning: a mixed alcoholic drink of spirit, fruit and spice
a blow that would make a fighter dazed, as grog (the original rum drink) makes one dizzy

explanation.definitionFit: A mixed drink made with spirit; also, read as an odd blow, a hit that dazes a fighter.

clue.text: By no means a crash helmet

definitions.text: By no means a crash helmet

parts.words: By no means a crash helmet
parts.note: a close-fitting soft cap worn on the crown of the head, which gives no protection in a crash

explanation.definitionFit: A small brimless cap covers the top of the head like a helmet but is made of soft cloth.

clue.text: Drink 'on the rocks, sweetie

parts.note: liquor is strong drink
a drink served on the rocks comes with ice

explanation.surface: A spirit poured over ice is a real treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetie' looks like a term of endearment but is a British word for a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A black chewy sweet flavoured with root extract is a confection.

clue.text: Sandy makes: Humpty take the count

definitions.text: Sandy makes: Humpty take the count

parts.words: Sandy makes: Humpty take the count
parts.note: a small hourglass full of sand counts the minutes while an egg (like Humpty Dumpty) boils

explanation.definitionFit: A small hourglass device measures how long an egg is boiled.

clue.text: General operations to pitch tents and gain new position

parts.note: to camp is to pitch tents

indicators.note: new position tells us the letters of gain are moved to fresh places

explanation.surface: Soldiers set up a tented base and then advance to new ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective meaning broad, but it is the army officer whose operations these are.
explanation.definitionFit: A military commander conducts a series of connected battles and manoeuvres in pursuit of a war aim.

clue.text: Sea-food first. on Molly's barrow

parts.note: Molly Malone, in the Irish song, wheels her barrow crying the shellfish named first in '... and mussels'

explanation.definitionFit: A small edible bivalve is the shellfish named first in Molly Malone's cry.

clue.text: Drink where one 'can hardly raise the elbow

definitions.meaning: a soft fruit cordial diluted with water

definitions.text: where one 'can hardly raise the elbow
definitions.meaning: a crush of people, so packed that nobody can lift a glass (raising the elbow is drinking)

explanation.definitionFit: A diluted fruit cordial is a soft drink, and a crowded crush leaves no room to lift an arm.

clue.text: Gammon, and the rest minced, pet.

parts.note: gammon is a cured ham

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so the letters of rest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bacon, with the remainder chopped up, is fed to the family animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gammon' looks like the British slang insult but is just cured pig meat; 'minced' scrambles the remainder word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent kept in a cage is a common household pet.

clue.text: Delicious hot-heads

parts.note: toasted teacakes served hot, whose tops are full of holes for butter; not short-tempered people

explanation.definitionFit: British spongy griddle cakes are toasted and eaten hot with butter soaking into their tops.

clue.text: Works of nature

definitions.meaning: a living thing that grows in the soil

explanation.definitionFit: A factory site is called by this word, as is any growing green organism.

clue.text: Weaver much sat-on

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
the part of the body one sits on

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream carries this name, and it is also the backside one sits on.

clue.text: The intention' he is lacking materially

indicators.note: lacking says the following word is taken away

parts.note: the will is the intention
taken as written

explanation.surface: His will is absent where it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes HE from THE WILL; 'materially' points to a cloth, the definition as a material.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven cloth with diagonal ribs is a fabric, so it is spoken of in material terms.

clue.text: Does Cowes. Week feature this craft?

indicators.note: the boat's name is a feature within the words Does Cowes, sitting across them

explanation.surface: Will this boat appear at the yachting regatta at Cowes?
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes Week is a yachting regatta held each August on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Miss Gray in 10

parts.note: Wordsworth's Lucy Gray, renamed as she would be in Italy (the answer to 10 across)

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian form of the girl's name Lucy, so Wordsworth's Lucy Gray would be called this in Italy.

clue.text: Sister Susie, factory hand

definitions.meaning: from the song 'Sister Susie's sewing shirts for soldiers', a sewer
a worker who operates a machine in a factory

explanation.definitionFit: The song's Sister Susie sews shirts, presumably at a sewing machine, and a factory operative works such a machine.

clue.text: Daisy on the .Mississippi

parts.note: not the flower but a riverboat on the great American river, driven by a paddle wheel at its back

explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer on American rivers was driven by one big wheel mounted at the rear.
